# gif package - github.com/freddyisaac/sicortex-golang/src/image/gif - Go Packages

Source: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/freddyisaac/sicortex-golang/src/image/gif

[¶](https://pkg.go.dev#section-documentation)

    ### Overview [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-overview)

Package gif implements a GIF image decoder and encoder.

The GIF specification is at [http://www.w3.org/Graphics/GIF/spec-gif89a.txt](http://www.w3.org/Graphics/GIF/spec-gif89a.txt).

### Index [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-index)

### Constants [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-constants)

  Disposal Methods.

### Variables [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-variables)

  This section is empty.

### Functions [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-functions)

  Decode reads a GIF image from r and returns the first embedded image as an image.Image.

####
      func [DecodeConfig](https://github.com/freddyisaac/sicortex-golang/blob/e03519e66f60/src/image/gif/reader.go#L524) [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#DecodeConfig)

  DecodeConfig returns the global color model and dimensions of a GIF image without decoding the entire image.

### Types [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-types)

  ```
type GIF struct {
	Image     []*
```
[image](https://pkg.go.dev/image).[Paletted](https://pkg.go.dev/image#Paletted) // The successive images.
	Delay     [][int](https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int)             // The successive delay times, one per frame, in 100ths of a second.
	LoopCount [int](https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int)               // The loop count.
	// Disposal is the successive disposal methods, one per frame. For
	// backwards compatibility, a nil Disposal is valid to pass to EncodeAll,
	// and implies that each frame's disposal method is 0 (no disposal
	// specified).
	Disposal [][byte](https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#byte)
	// Config is the global color table (palette), width and height. A nil or
	// empty-color.Palette Config.ColorModel means that each frame has its own
	// color table and there is no global color table. Each frame's bounds must
	// be within the rectangle defined by the two points (0, 0) and
	// (Config.Width, Config.Height).
	//
	// For backwards compatibility, a zero-valued Config is valid to pass to
	// EncodeAll, and implies that the overall GIF's width and height equals
	// the first frame's bounds' Rectangle.Max point.
	Config [image](https://pkg.go.dev/image).[Config](https://pkg.go.dev/image#Config)
	// BackgroundIndex is the background index in the global color table, for
	// use with the DisposalBackground disposal method.
	BackgroundIndex [byte](https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#byte)
}
    GIF represents the possibly multiple images stored in a GIF file.

```
type Options struct {
	// NumColors is the maximum number of colors used in the image.
	// It ranges from 1 to 256.
	NumColors
```
[int](https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int)
	// Quantizer is used to produce a palette with size NumColors.
	// palette.Plan9 is used in place of a nil Quantizer.
	Quantizer [draw](https://pkg.go.dev/image/draw).[Quantizer](https://pkg.go.dev/image/draw#Quantizer)
	// Drawer is used to convert the source image to the desired palette.
	// draw.FloydSteinberg is used in place of a nil Drawer.

}

  ####
      func [CheckUserDomain](https://github.com/freeflowuniverse/freeflow_teams_backend/blob/v5.11.1/app/user.go#L361) [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#CheckUserDomain)

  CheckUserDomain checks that a user's email domain matches a list of space-delimited domains as a string.

Given a post returns the values of the fields in which mentions are possible. post.message, preText and text in the attachment are enabled.

      func (*Server) [AddClusterLeaderChangedListener](https://github.com/freeflowuniverse/freeflow_teams_backend/blob/v5.11.1/app/cluster.go#L13) [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#Server.AddClusterLeaderChangedListener)

  Registers a given function to be called when the cluster leader may have changed. Returns a unique ID for the listener which can later be used to remove it. If clustering is not enabled in this build, the callback will never be called.

####
      func (*Server) [AddConfigListener](https://github.com/freeflowuniverse/freeflow_teams_backend/blob/v5.11.1/app/config.go#L89) [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#Server.AddConfigListener)

  Registers a function with a given to be called when the config is reloaded and may have changed. The function will be called with two arguments: the old config and the new config. AddConfigListener returns a unique ID for the listener that can later be used to remove it.

####
      func (*Server) [AsymmetricSigningKey](https://github.com/freeflowuniverse/freeflow_teams_backend/blob/v5.11.1/app/config.go#L265) [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#Server.AsymmetricSigningKey)

  AsymmetricSigningKey will return a private key that can be used for asymmetric signing.

A temporary bridge to deal with cases where the code is so tighly coupled that this is easier as a temporary solution

Go creates a goroutine, but maintains a record of it to ensure that execution completes before the server is shutdown.

    UploadFileX uploads a single file as specified in t. It applies the upload constraints, executes plugins and image processing logic as needed.     ####
      func (*Server) [AddClusterLeaderChangedListener](https://github.com/fretkak/mattermost-mattermost-server/blob/v5.11.1/app/cluster.go#L13) [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#Server.AddClusterLeaderChangedListener)

  Registers a given function to be called when the cluster leader may have changed. Returns a unique ID for the listener which can later be used to remove it. If clustering is not enabled in this build, the callback will never be called.

####
      func (*Server) [AddConfigListener](https://github.com/fretkak/mattermost-mattermost-server/blob/v5.11.1/app/config.go#L89) [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#Server.AddConfigListener)

  Registers a function with a given to be called when the config is reloaded and may have changed. The function will be called with two arguments: the old config and the new config. AddConfigListener returns a unique ID for the listener that can later be used to remove it.

####
      func (*Server) [AppOptions](https://github.com/fretkak/mattermost-mattermost-server/blob/v5.11.1/app/server.go#L271) [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#Server.AppOptions)

  Global app opptions that should be applied to apps created by this server

####
      func (*Server) [AsymmetricSigningKey](https://github.com/fretkak/mattermost-mattermost-server/blob/v5.11.1/app/config.go#L265) [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#Server.AsymmetricSigningKey)

  AsymmetricSigningKey will return a private key that can be used for asymmetric signing.

A temporary bridge to deal with cases where the code is so tighly coupled that this is easier as a temporary solution

Go creates a goroutine, but maintains a record of it to ensure that execution completes before the server is shutdown.

####
      func (*Server) [RemoveClusterLeaderChangedListener](https://github.com/fretkak/mattermost-mattermost-server/blob/v5.11.1/app/cluster.go#L20) [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#Server.RemoveClusterLeaderChangedListener)

####
      func (*Server) [RunOldAppInitalization](https://github.com/fretkak/mattermost-mattermost-server/blob/v5.11.1/app/server_app_adapters.go#L25) [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#Server.RunOldAppInitalization)

  This is a bridge between the old and new initalization for the context refactor. It calls app layer initalization code that then turns around and acts on the server. Don't add anything new here, new initilization should be done in the server and performed in the NewServer function.

# textimg command - github.com/jiro4989/textimg - Go Packages

Source: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/jiro4989/textimg

README
      [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#section-readme)

      ### textimg

textimg is command to convert from color text (ANSI or 256) to image. + Drawn image keeps having colors of escape sequence.

#### Development

go version go1.12 linux/amd64

**I didn't test on Windows.**

#### Usage examples

##### Simple examples

```
textimg $'\x1b[31mRED\x1b[0m' > out.png
textimg $'\x1b[31mRED\x1b[0m' -o out.png
echo -e '\x1b[31mRED\x1b[0m' | textimg -o out.png
echo -e '\x1b[31mRED\x1b[0m' | textimg --background 0,255,255,255 -o out.jpg
echo -e '\x1b[31mRED\x1b[0m' | textimg --background black -o out.gif
```
Output image format is PNG or JPG or GIF.
File extention of `-o` option defines output image format.
Default image format is PNG. if you write image file with `>` redirect then
image file will be saved as PNG file.

##### Rainbow examples

###### From ANSI color

textimg supports `\x1b[30m` notation.

```
colors=(30 31 32 33 34 35 36 37)
i=0
while read -r line; do
  echo -e "$line" | sed -r 's/.*/\x1b['"${colors[$((i%8))]}"'m&\x1b[m/g'
  i=$((i+1))
done <<< "$(seq 8 | xargs -I@ echo TEST)" | textimg -b 50,100,12,255 -o testdata/out/rainbow.png
```
Output is here.

###### From 256 color

textimg supports `\x1b[38;5;255m` notation.

Foreground example is below.

```
seq 0 255 | while read -r i; do
  echo -ne "\x1b[38;5;${i}m$(printf %03d $i)"
  if [ $(((i+1) % 16)) -eq 0 ]; then
    echo
  fi
done | textimg -o 256_fg.png
```
Output is here.

Background example is below.

```
seq 0 255 | while read -r i; do
  echo -ne "\x1b[48;5;${i}m$(printf %03d $i)"
  if [ $(((i+1) % 16)) -eq 0 ]; then
    echo
  fi
done | textimg -o 256_bg.png
```
Output is here.

###### From 256 RGB color

textimg supports `\x1b[38;2;255;0;0m` notation.

```
seq 0 255 | while read i; do
  echo -ne "\x1b[38;2;${i};0;0m$(printf %03d $i)"
  if [ $(((i+1) % 16)) -eq 0 ]; then
    echo
  fi
done | textimg -o extrgb_f_gradation.png
```
Output is here.

###### Animation GIF

textimg supports animation GIF.

```
echo -e '\x1b[31mText\x1b[0m
\x1b[32mText\x1b[0m
\x1b[33mText\x1b[0m
\x1b[34mText\x1b[0m
\x1b[35mText\x1b[0m
\x1b[36mText\x1b[0m
\x1b[37mText\x1b[0m
\x1b[41mText\x1b[0m
\x1b[42mText\x1b[0m
\x1b[43mText\x1b[0m
\x1b[44mText\x1b[0m
\x1b[45mText\x1b[0m
\x1b[46mText\x1b[0m
\x1b[47mText\x1b[0m' | textimg -a -o ansi_fb_anime_1line.gif
```
Output is here.

###### Slide animation GIF

```
echo -e '\x1b[31mText\x1b[0m
\x1b[32mText\x1b[0m
\x1b[33mText\x1b[0m
\x1b[34mText\x1b[0m
\x1b[35mText\x1b[0m
\x1b[36mText\x1b[0m
\x1b[37mText\x1b[0m
\x1b[41mText\x1b[0m
\x1b[42mText\x1b[0m
\x1b[43mText\x1b[0m
\x1b[44mText\x1b[0m
\x1b[45mText\x1b[0m
\x1b[46mText\x1b[0m
\x1b[47mText\x1b[0m' | textimg -l 5 -SE -o slide_5_1_rainbow_forever.gif
```
Output is here.

##### Using on Docker

You can use textimg on Docker.

```
docker pull jiro4989/textimg
docker run -v $(pwd):/images -it jiro4989/textimg -h
docker run -v $(pwd):/images -it jiro4989/textimg Testあいうえお😄 -o /images/a.png
docker run -v $(pwd):/images -it jiro4989/textimg Testあいうえお😄 -s
```
#### Install

```
go get -u github.com/jiro4989/textimg
```
or

Download binary from [Releases](https://github.com/jiro4989/textimg/releases).

#### Help

```
textimg is command to convert from colored text (ANSI or 256) to image.
Usage:
  textimg [flags]
Examples:
textimg $'\x1b[31mRED\x1b[0m' -o out.png
Flags:
      --foreground string         foreground color.
                                  format is [black|red|green|yellow|blue|magenta|cyan|white]
                                  or (R,G,B,A(0~255)) (default "white")
  -b, --background string         ackground color.
                                  color format is same as "foreground" option (default "black")
  -f, --fontfile string           font file path.
                                  You can change this default value with environment variables TEXTIMG_FONT_FILE (default "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/hack-gen/HackGen-Regular.ttf")
  -e, --emoji-fontfile string     emoji font file (default "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/symbola/Symbola_hint.ttf")
  -i, --use-emoji-font            use emoji font
  -z, --shellgei-emoji-fontfile   emoji font file for shellgei-bot (path: "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/ancient-scripts/Symbola_hint.ttf")
  -F, --fontsize int              font size (default 20)
  -o, --out string                output image file path.
                                  available image formats are [png | jpg | gif]
  -s, --shellgei-imagedir         image directory path for shellgei-bot (path: "/images/t.png")
  -a, --animation                 generate animation gif
  -d, --delay int                 animation delay time (default 20)
  -l, --line-count int            animation input line count (default 1)
  -S, --slide                     use slide animation
  -W, --slide-width int           sliding animation width (default 1)
  -E, --forever                   sliding forever
      --environments              print environment variables
  -h, --help                      help for textimg
      --version                   version for textimg
```
#### Fonts

##### Default font path

Default fonts that to use are below.

| OS | Font path |
|---|---|
| Linux | /usr/share/fonts/truetype/vlgothic/VL-Gothic-Regular.ttf |
| MacOS | /Library/Fonts/AppleGothic.ttf |
| Windows | Not supported (Welcome Pull Request!) |

You can change this font path with environment variables `TEXTIMG_FONT_FILE` .

Examples.

```
export TEXTIMG_FONT_FILE=/usr/share/fonts/TTF/HackGen-Regular.ttf
```
##### Emoji font (image file path)

textimg needs emoji image files to draw emoji.
You have to set `TEXTIMG_EMOJI_DIR` environment variables if you want to draw
one.
For example, run below.

```
# You can clone your favorite fonts here.
sudo git clone https://github.com/googlefonts/noto-emoji /usr/local/src/noto-emoji
export TEXTIMG_EMOJI_DIR=/usr/local/src/noto-emoji/png/128
echo Test👍 | textimg -o emoji.png
```
##### Emoji font (TTF)

textimg can change emoji font with `TEXTIMG_EMOJI_FONT_FILE` environment variables and set `-i` option.
For example, swicthing emoji font to [Symbola font](https://www.wfonts.com/font/symbola).

```
export TEXTIMG_EMOJI_FONT_FILE=/usr/share/fonts/TTF/Symbola.ttf
echo あ😃a👍！👀ん👄 | textimg -i -o emoji_symbola.png
```

####
      func (*App) [AddClusterLeaderChangedListener](https://github.com/jlevesy/mattermost-server/blob/v5.3.1/app/cluster.go#L11) [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#App.AddClusterLeaderChangedListener)

  Registers a given function to be called when the cluster leader may have changed. Returns a unique ID for the listener which can later be used to remove it. If clustering is not enabled in this build, the callback will never be called.

####
      func (*App) [AddConfigListener](https://github.com/jlevesy/mattermost-server/blob/v5.3.1/app/config.go#L121) [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#App.AddConfigListener)

  Registers a function with a given to be called when the config is reloaded and may have changed. The function will be called with two arguments: the old config and the new config. AddConfigListener returns a unique ID for the listener that can later be used to remove it.

####
      func [RecordScreenAsGIF](https://github.com/jnjackins/ebiten/blob/v1.1.0/ebitenutil/gif.go#L130) [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#RecordScreenAsGIF)

    RecordScreenAsGIF returns updating function with recording the screen as an animation GIF image.

This encodes each screen at each frame and may slows the application.

Here is the example to record initial 120 frames of your game:

```
func update(screen *ebiten.Image) error {
    // ...
}
func main() {
    out, err := os.Create("output.gif")
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    defer out.Close()
    update := RecordScreenAsGIF(update, out, 120)
    if err := ebiten.Run(update, 320, 240, 2, "Your game's title"); err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
}
```

# gif package - github.com/jocgir/go/src/image/gif - Go Packages

Source: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/jocgir/go/src/image/gif

[¶](https://pkg.go.dev#section-documentation)

    ### Overview [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-overview)

Package gif implements a GIF image decoder and encoder.

The GIF specification is at [https://www.w3.org/Graphics/GIF/spec-gif89a.txt](https://www.w3.org/Graphics/GIF/spec-gif89a.txt).

### Index [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-index)

### Constants [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-constants)

  Disposal Methods.

### Variables [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-variables)

  This section is empty.

### Functions [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-functions)

  Decode reads a GIF image from r and returns the first embedded image as an image.Image.

####
      func [DecodeConfig](https://github.com/jocgir/go/blob/b84a58095f11/src/image/gif/reader.go#L623) [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#DecodeConfig)

  DecodeConfig returns the global color model and dimensions of a GIF image without decoding the entire image.

### Types [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-types)

  ```
type GIF struct {
	Image []*
```
[image](https://pkg.go.dev/image).[Paletted](https://pkg.go.dev/image#Paletted) // The successive images.
	Delay [][int](https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int)             // The successive delay times, one per frame, in 100ths of a second.
	// LoopCount controls the number of times an animation will be
	// restarted during display.
	// A LoopCount of 0 means to loop forever.
	// A LoopCount of -1 means to show each frame only once.
	// Otherwise, the animation is looped LoopCount+1 times.
	LoopCount [int](https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int)
	// Disposal is the successive disposal methods, one per frame. For
	// backwards compatibility, a nil Disposal is valid to pass to EncodeAll,
	// and implies that each frame's disposal method is 0 (no disposal
	// specified).
	Disposal [][byte](https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#byte)
	// Config is the global color table (palette), width and height. A nil or
	// empty-color.Palette Config.ColorModel means that each frame has its own
	// color table and there is no global color table. Each frame's bounds must
	// be within the rectangle defined by the two points (0, 0) and
	// (Config.Width, Config.Height).
	//
	// For backwards compatibility, a zero-valued Config is valid to pass to
	// EncodeAll, and implies that the overall GIF's width and height equals
	// the first frame's bounds' Rectangle.Max point.
	Config [image](https://pkg.go.dev/image).[Config](https://pkg.go.dev/image#Config)
	// BackgroundIndex is the background index in the global color table, for
	// use with the DisposalBackground disposal method.
	BackgroundIndex [byte](https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#byte)
}
    GIF represents the possibly multiple images stored in a GIF file.

```
type Options struct {
	// NumColors is the maximum number of colors used in the image.
	// It ranges from 1 to 256.
	NumColors
```
[int](https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int)
	// Quantizer is used to produce a palette with size NumColors.
	// palette.Plan9 is used in place of a nil Quantizer.
	Quantizer [draw](https://pkg.go.dev/image/draw).[Quantizer](https://pkg.go.dev/image/draw#Quantizer)
	// Drawer is used to convert the source image to the desired palette.
	// draw.FloydSteinberg is used in place of a nil Drawer.
	Drawer [draw](https://pkg.go.dev/image/draw).[Drawer](https://pkg.go.dev/image/draw#Drawer)
}
    Options are the encoding parameters.

####
      func [NewImageFromFile](https://github.com/joeblew99/ebiten/blob/v1.5.0/ebitenutil/loadimage.go#L32) [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#NewImageFromFile)

  NewImageFromFile loads the file path and returns ebiten.Image and image.Image.

The current directory for path depends on your environment. This will vary on your desktop or web browser. Note that this doesn't work on mobiles. It'll be safer to embed your resource, e.g., with github.com/jteeuwen/go-bindata instead of using this function.

### Functions [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-functions)

  ####
      func [DebugPrint](https://github.com/johnsto/ebiten/blob/v1.6.1/ebitenutil/debugprint.go#L36) [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#DebugPrint)

  DebugPrint draws the string str on the image.

DebugPrint always returns nil as of 1.5.0-alpha.

DrawLine draws a line segment on the given destination dst.

DrawLine is intended to be used mainly for debugging or prototyping purpose.

DrawRect draws a rectangle on the given destination dst.

DrawRect is intended to be used mainly for debugging or prototyping purpose.

####
      func [NewImageFromFile](https://github.com/johnsto/ebiten/blob/v1.6.1/ebitenutil/loadimage.go#L33) [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#NewImageFromFile)

  NewImageFromFile loads the file with path and returns ebiten.Image and image.Image.

How to solve path depends on your environment. This varies on your desktop or web browser. Note that this doesn't work on mobiles.

For productions, instead of using this function, it is safer to embed your resources, e.g., with github.com/jteeuwen/go-bindata .

####
      func [RecordScreenAsGIF](https://github.com/johnsto/ebiten/blob/v1.6.1/ebitenutil/gif.go#L131) [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#RecordScreenAsGIF)

    RecordScreenAsGIF is deprecated as of version 1.6.0-alpha.

RecordScreenAsGIF returns updating function with recording the screen as an animation GIF image.

This encodes each screen at each frame and may slows the application.

Here is the example to record initial 120 frames of your game:

```
func update(screen *ebiten.Image) error {
    // ...
}
func main() {
    out, err := os.Create("output.gif")
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    defer out.Close()
    update := RecordScreenAsGIF(update, out, 120)
    if err := ebiten.Run(update, 320, 240, 2, "Your game's title"); err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
}
```

        ### Types [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-types)

      v1.3.0

  ReadSeekCloser is io.ReadSeeker and io.Closer.

# gif package - github.com/jonasi/go/src/image/gif - Go Packages

Source: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/jonasi/go/src/image/gif

[¶](https://pkg.go.dev#section-documentation)

    ### Overview [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-overview)

Package gif implements a GIF image decoder and encoder.

The GIF specification is at [http://www.w3.org/Graphics/GIF/spec-gif89a.txt](http://www.w3.org/Graphics/GIF/spec-gif89a.txt).

### Index [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-index)

### Constants [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-constants)

  Disposal Methods.

### Variables [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-variables)

  This section is empty.

### Functions [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-functions)

  Decode reads a GIF image from r and returns the first embedded image as an image.Image.

####
      func [DecodeConfig](https://github.com/jonasi/go/blob/e78e654c1de0/src/image/gif/reader.go#L480) [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#DecodeConfig)

  DecodeConfig returns the global color model and dimensions of a GIF image without decoding the entire image.

### Types [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-types)

  ```
type GIF struct {
	Image     []*
```
[image](https://pkg.go.dev/image).[Paletted](https://pkg.go.dev/image#Paletted) // The successive images.
	Delay     [][int](https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int)             // The successive delay times, one per frame, in 100ths of a second.
	LoopCount [int](https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int)               // The loop count.
	// Disposal is the successive disposal methods, one per frame. For
	// backwards compatibility, a nil Disposal is valid to pass to EncodeAll,
	// and implies that each frame's disposal method is 0 (no disposal
	// specified).
	Disposal [][byte](https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#byte)
	// Config is the global color table (palette), width and height. A nil or
	// empty-color.Palette Config.ColorModel means that each frame has its own
	// color table and there is no global color table. Each frame's bounds must
	// be within the rectangle defined by the two points (0, 0) and
	// (Config.Width, Config.Height).
	//
	// For backwards compatibility, a zero-valued Config is valid to pass to
	// EncodeAll, and implies that the overall GIF's width and height equals
	// the first frame's bounds' Rectangle.Max point.
	Config [image](https://pkg.go.dev/image).[Config](https://pkg.go.dev/image#Config)
	// BackgroundIndex is the background index in the global color table, for
	// use with the DisposalBackground disposal method.
	BackgroundIndex [byte](https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#byte)
}
    GIF represents the possibly multiple images stored in a GIF file.

```
type Options struct {
	// NumColors is the maximum number of colors used in the image.
	// It ranges from 1 to 256.
	NumColors
```
[int](https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int)
	// Quantizer is used to produce a palette with size NumColors.
	// palette.Plan9 is used in place of a nil Quantizer.
	Quantizer [draw](https://pkg.go.dev/image/draw).[Quantizer](https://pkg.go.dev/image/draw#Quantizer)
	// Drawer is used to convert the source image to the desired palette.
	// draw.FloydSteinberg is used in place of a nil Drawer.
	Drawer [draw](https://pkg.go.dev/image/draw).[Drawer](https://pkg.go.dev/image/draw#Drawer)
}
    Options are the encoding parameters.

      func [UseTestStore](https://github.com/jumuro-dev/mattermost-server/blob/v4.10.10/api/apitestlib.go#L55) [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#UseTestStore)

  UseTestStore sets the container and corresponding settings to use for tests. Once the tests are complete (e.g. at the end of your TestMain implementation), you should call StopTestStore.

# gif package - github.com/motemen/go/src/image/gif - Go Packages

Source: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/motemen/go/src/image/gif

[¶](https://pkg.go.dev#section-documentation)

    ### Overview [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-overview)

Package gif implements a GIF image decoder and encoder.

The GIF specification is at [http://www.w3.org/Graphics/GIF/spec-gif89a.txt](http://www.w3.org/Graphics/GIF/spec-gif89a.txt).

### Index [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-index)

### Constants [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-constants)

  Disposal Methods.

### Variables [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-variables)

  This section is empty.

### Functions [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-functions)

  Decode reads a GIF image from r and returns the first embedded image as an image.Image.

####
      func [DecodeConfig](https://github.com/motemen/go/blob/262b524a1171/src/image/gif/reader.go#L623) [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#DecodeConfig)

  DecodeConfig returns the global color model and dimensions of a GIF image without decoding the entire image.

### Types [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-types)

  ```
type GIF struct {
	Image []*
```
[image](https://pkg.go.dev/image).[Paletted](https://pkg.go.dev/image#Paletted) // The successive images.
	Delay [][int](https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int)             // The successive delay times, one per frame, in 100ths of a second.
	// LoopCount controls the number of times an animation will be
	// restarted during display.
	// A LoopCount of 0 means to loop forever.
	// A LoopCount of -1 means to show each frame only once.
	// Otherwise, the animation is looped LoopCount+1 times.
	LoopCount [int](https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int)
	// Disposal is the successive disposal methods, one per frame. For
	// backwards compatibility, a nil Disposal is valid to pass to EncodeAll,
	// and implies that each frame's disposal method is 0 (no disposal
	// specified).
	Disposal [][byte](https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#byte)
	// Config is the global color table (palette), width and height. A nil or
	// empty-color.Palette Config.ColorModel means that each frame has its own
	// color table and there is no global color table. Each frame's bounds must
	// be within the rectangle defined by the two points (0, 0) and
	// (Config.Width, Config.Height).
	//
	// For backwards compatibility, a zero-valued Config is valid to pass to
	// EncodeAll, and implies that the overall GIF's width and height equals
	// the first frame's bounds' Rectangle.Max point.
	Config [image](https://pkg.go.dev/image).[Config](https://pkg.go.dev/image#Config)
	// BackgroundIndex is the background index in the global color table, for
	// use with the DisposalBackground disposal method.
	BackgroundIndex [byte](https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#byte)
}
    GIF represents the possibly multiple images stored in a GIF file.

```
type Options struct {
	// NumColors is the maximum number of colors used in the image.
	// It ranges from 1 to 256.
	NumColors
```
[int](https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int)
	// Quantizer is used to produce a palette with size NumColors.
	// palette.Plan9 is used in place of a nil Quantizer.
	Quantizer [draw](https://pkg.go.dev/image/draw).[Quantizer](https://pkg.go.dev/image/draw#Quantizer)
	// Drawer is used to convert the source image to the desired palette.
	// draw.FloydSteinberg is used in place of a nil Drawer.
	Drawer [draw](https://pkg.go.dev/image/draw).[Drawer](https://pkg.go.dev/image/draw#Drawer)
}
    Options are the encoding parameters.

####
      func (*Package) [DefaultName](https://github.com/muazhari/gomacro-custom/blob/a6136ef7aaa6/imports/a_package.go#L101) [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#Package.DefaultName)

  *

- return the default name to bind when importing Package *
- [https://golang.org/ref/spec#Package_clause](https://golang.org/ref/spec#Package_clause)states:
- If the PackageName is omitted, it defaults to the identifier
- specified in the package clause of the imported package *
- So use that if known, otherwise extrapolate it from package path

# gif package - github.com/muesli/go/src/image/gif - Go Packages

Source: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/muesli/go/src/image/gif

[¶](https://pkg.go.dev#section-documentation)

    ### Overview [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-overview)

Package gif implements a GIF image decoder and encoder.

The GIF specification is at [http://www.w3.org/Graphics/GIF/spec-gif89a.txt](http://www.w3.org/Graphics/GIF/spec-gif89a.txt).

### Index [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-index)

### Constants [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-constants)

  Disposal Methods.

### Variables [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-variables)

  This section is empty.

### Functions [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-functions)

  Decode reads a GIF image from r and returns the first embedded image as an image.Image.

####
      func [DecodeConfig](https://github.com/muesli/go/blob/e410d2a81ef2/src/image/gif/reader.go#L524) [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#DecodeConfig)

  DecodeConfig returns the global color model and dimensions of a GIF image without decoding the entire image.

### Types [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-types)

  ```
type GIF struct {
	Image     []*
```
[image](https://pkg.go.dev/image).[Paletted](https://pkg.go.dev/image#Paletted) // The successive images.
	Delay     [][int](https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int)             // The successive delay times, one per frame, in 100ths of a second.
	LoopCount [int](https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int)               // The loop count.
	// Disposal is the successive disposal methods, one per frame. For
	// backwards compatibility, a nil Disposal is valid to pass to EncodeAll,
	// and implies that each frame's disposal method is 0 (no disposal
	// specified).
	Disposal [][byte](https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#byte)
	// Config is the global color table (palette), width and height. A nil or
	// empty-color.Palette Config.ColorModel means that each frame has its own
	// color table and there is no global color table. Each frame's bounds must
	// be within the rectangle defined by the two points (0, 0) and
	// (Config.Width, Config.Height).
	//
	// For backwards compatibility, a zero-valued Config is valid to pass to
	// EncodeAll, and implies that the overall GIF's width and height equals
	// the first frame's bounds' Rectangle.Max point.
	Config [image](https://pkg.go.dev/image).[Config](https://pkg.go.dev/image#Config)
	// BackgroundIndex is the background index in the global color table, for
	// use with the DisposalBackground disposal method.
	BackgroundIndex [byte](https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#byte)
}
    GIF represents the possibly multiple images stored in a GIF file.

```
type Options struct {
	// NumColors is the maximum number of colors used in the image.
	// It ranges from 1 to 256.
	NumColors
```
[int](https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int)
	// Quantizer is used to produce a palette with size NumColors.
	// palette.Plan9 is used in place of a nil Quantizer.
	Quantizer [draw](https://pkg.go.dev/image/draw).[Quantizer](https://pkg.go.dev/image/draw#Quantizer)
	// Drawer is used to convert the source image to the desired palette.
	// draw.FloydSteinberg is used in place of a nil Drawer.
	Drawer [draw](https://pkg.go.dev/image/draw).[Drawer](https://pkg.go.dev/image/draw#Drawer)
}
    Options are the encoding parameters.

go-sparkline --help

Help

$ go-sparkline --help
usage: go-sparkline [<flags>] [<values>]
Flags:
--help Show help.
-s, --stream stream
--animate start animation
--lazy ignore parse errors
--char-size=7:17 Pixel size of a single character. Can also be set via env
ITERM_CHARACTER_SIZE. The default 7:17 corresponds to 12p Monaco.
--rows=3 height in number of rows
--renderer=sparks available renderers: line, sparks, vlines
Args:
[<values>] Numeric values to render. Can also be read from stdin.

### Constants [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-constants)

  ### Variables [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-variables)

  ErrAbortOnPartMismatch is returned when there is a mismatch between a current part and a previous attempt part. If ErrAbortOnPartMismatch is returned, the caller should abort the upload attempt and start from scratch.

All devices are presumed active for the first 24 hours. See comment below.

####
      func (*Boxer) [UnboxMessage](https://github.com/nailanawshaba/shasthohub/blob/v1.0.40/go/chat/boxer.go#L206) [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#Boxer.UnboxMessage)

    func (b *[Boxer](https://pkg.go.dev#Boxer)) UnboxMessage(ctx[context](https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/net/context).[Context](https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/net/context#Context), boxed[chat1](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/keybase/client/go/protocol/chat1).[MessageBoxed](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/keybase/client/go/protocol/chat1#MessageBoxed), conv unboxConversationInfo) (m[chat1](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/keybase/client/go/protocol/chat1).[MessageUnboxed](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/keybase/client/go/protocol/chat1#MessageUnboxed), uberr[UnboxingError](https://pkg.go.dev#UnboxingError))

UnboxMessage unboxes a chat1.MessageBoxed into a chat1.MessageUnboxed. It finds the appropriate keybase1.CryptKey, decrypts the message, and verifies several things:

- The message's signature is valid.
- (TODO) The signing KID was valid when the signature was made.
- (TODO) The signing KID belongs to the sending device.
- (TODO) The sending device belongs to the sender. [Note that we do currently check the KID -> UID relationship, independent of the device ID.]
- (TODO) The sender has write permission in the TLF.
- (TODO) The TLF name, public flag, and finalized info resolve to the TLF ID.
- The conversation ID derives from the ConversationIDTriple.
- The body hash is not a replay from another message we know about.
- The prev pointers are consistent with other messages we know about.
- (TODO) The prev pointers are not absurdly ancient.
- The ClientHeader provided with the BoxedMessage matches the one we decrypt.

The first return value is unusable if the err != nil. Returns (_, err) for non-permanent errors, and (MessageUnboxedError, nil) for permanent errors. Permanent errors can be cached and must be treated as a value to deal with, whereas temporary errors are transient failures.

      type [ChatThreadConsistencyError](https://github.com/nailanawshaba/shasthohub/blob/v1.0.40/go/chat/errors.go#L77) [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#ChatThreadConsistencyError)

func CheckPrevPointersAndGetUnpreved(thread *[chat1](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/keybase/client/go/protocol/chat1).[ThreadView](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/keybase/client/go/protocol/chat1#ThreadView)) ([][chat1](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/keybase/client/go/protocol/chat1).[MessagePreviousPointer](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/keybase/client/go/protocol/chat1#MessagePreviousPointer),[ChatThreadConsistencyError](https://pkg.go.dev#ChatThreadConsistencyError))

Ingest a ThreadView, check several invariants, and produce a list of prev pointers to not-yet-pointed-to messages. Check several invariants at the same time: 1. No two messages have the same ID. 2. All prev pointers point to messages with lesser IDs. 3. All prev pointers to a message agree on that message's header hash. 4. For all messages we have locally, the hashes pointing to them are actually correct. TODO: All of this should happen in the cache instead of here all at once.

    FetchRetrier is responsible for tracking any nonblock fetch failures, and retrying them automatically.

Connected is called when a connection to the chat server is established, and forces a pass over the retry queue

####

func (f *[FetchRetrier](https://pkg.go.dev#FetchRetrier)) Failure(ctx[context](https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/net/context).[Context](https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/net/context#Context), uid[gregor1](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/keybase/client/go/protocol/gregor1).[UID](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/keybase/client/go/protocol/gregor1#UID), desc[types](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/keybase/client/go/chat/types).[RetryDescription](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/keybase/client/go/chat/types#RetryDescription)) (err[error](https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error))

IsOffline returns if the module thinks we are connected to the chat server.

### Functions [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-functions)

  ####
      func [DebugPrint](https://github.com/nanoslayer/ebiten/blob/v1.6.4/ebitenutil/debugprint.go#L36) [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#DebugPrint)

  DebugPrint draws the string str on the image.

DebugPrint always returns nil as of 1.5.0-alpha.

DrawLine draws a line segment on the given destination dst.

DrawLine is intended to be used mainly for debugging or prototyping purpose.

DrawRect draws a rectangle on the given destination dst.

DrawRect is intended to be used mainly for debugging or prototyping purpose.

####
      func [NewImageFromFile](https://github.com/nanoslayer/ebiten/blob/v1.6.4/ebitenutil/loadimage.go#L33) [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#NewImageFromFile)

  NewImageFromFile loads the file with path and returns ebiten.Image and image.Image.

How to solve path depends on your environment. This varies on your desktop or web browser. Note that this doesn't work on mobiles.

For productions, instead of using this function, it is safer to embed your resources, e.g., with github.com/jteeuwen/go-bindata .

####
      func [RecordScreenAsGIF](https://github.com/nanoslayer/ebiten/blob/v1.6.4/ebitenutil/gif.go#L131) [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#RecordScreenAsGIF)

    RecordScreenAsGIF is deprecated as of version 1.6.0-alpha.

RecordScreenAsGIF returns updating function with recording the screen as an animation GIF image.

This encodes each screen at each frame and may slows the application.

Here is the example to record initial 120 frames of your game:

```
func update(screen *ebiten.Image) error {
    // ...
}
func main() {
    out, err := os.Create("output.gif")
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    defer out.Close()
    update := RecordScreenAsGIF(update, out, 120)
    if err := ebiten.Run(update, 320, 240, 2, "Your game's title"); err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
}
```

# ebitenutil package - github.com/nekketsuuu/ebiten/ebitenutil - Go Packages

[¶](https://pkg.go.dev#section-documentation)

      ### Index [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-index)

### Constants [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-constants)

  This section is empty.

### Variables [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-variables)

  This section is empty.

### Functions [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-functions)

  ####
      func [NewImageFromFile](https://github.com/nekketsuuu/ebiten/blob/v1.3.0/ebitenutil/loadimage.go#L27) [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#NewImageFromFile)

  NewImageFromFile loads the file path and returns ebiten.Image and image.Image.

The current directory for path depends on your environment. This will vary on your desktop or web browser. It'll be safer to embed your resource, e.g., with github.com/jteeuwen/go-bindata instead of using this function.

####
      func [RecordScreenAsGIF](https://github.com/nekketsuuu/ebiten/blob/v1.3.0/ebitenutil/gif.go#L129) [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#RecordScreenAsGIF)

    RecordScreenAsGIF returns updating function with recording the screen as an animation GIF image.

This encodes each screen at each frame and may slows the application.

Here is the example to record initial 120 frames of your game:

```
func update(screen *ebiten.Image) error {
    // ...
}
func main() {
    out, err := os.Create("output.gif")
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    defer out.Close()
    update := RecordScreenAsGIF(update, out, 120)
    if err := ebiten.Run(update, 320, 240, 2, "Your game's title"); err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
}
```

# gif package - github.com/nektro/go14/src/image/gif - Go Packages

Source: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/nektro/go14/src/image/gif

[¶](https://pkg.go.dev#section-documentation)

    ### Overview [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-overview)

Package gif implements a GIF image decoder and encoder.

The GIF specification is at [http://www.w3.org/Graphics/GIF/spec-gif89a.txt](http://www.w3.org/Graphics/GIF/spec-gif89a.txt).

### Index [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-index)

### Constants [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-constants)

  This section is empty.

### Variables [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-variables)

  This section is empty.

### Functions [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-functions)

  Decode reads a GIF image from r and returns the first embedded image as an image.Image.

####
      func [DecodeConfig](https://github.com/nektro/go14/blob/5976d0794628/src/image/gif/reader.go#L451) [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#DecodeConfig)

  DecodeConfig returns the global color model and dimensions of a GIF image without decoding the entire image.

### Types [¶](https://pkg.go.dev#pkg-types)

  ```
type GIF struct {
	Image     []*
```
[image](https://pkg.go.dev/image).[Paletted](https://pkg.go.dev/image#Paletted) // The successive images.
	Delay     [][int](https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int)             // The successive delay times, one per frame, in 100ths of a second.
	LoopCount [int](https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int)               // The loop count.
}
    GIF represents the possibly multiple images stored in a GIF file.

```
type Options struct {
	// NumColors is the maximum number of colors used in the image.
	// It ranges from 1 to 256.
	NumColors
```
[int](https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int)
	// Quantizer is used to produce a palette with size NumColors.

	Quantizer [draw](https://pkg.go.dev/image/draw).[Quantizer](https://pkg.go.dev/image/draw#Quantizer)
	// Drawer is used to convert the source image to the desired palette.

    Options are the encoding parameters.
